# Arusha Wildlife Safaris: full reference

Arusha Wildlife Safaris is a Tanzania safari and Kilimanjaro trekking operator based at
Njiro Road, Arusha, Tanzania, founded in 2014. Explore Tanzania · Experience the Wild. All figures below are the
operator's own published values. Website: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com

## How the company operates

- Private departures only. No shared group trips.
- Nine Land Cruisers owned outright and serviced in the company workshop every 5,000 km.
- Guides employed on annual salary, average tenure seven years, all holding Tanzanian professional guide licences.
- Park fees, concession fees and full board are itemised in every quote.
- Deposit is 30% on confirmation, balance 45 days before arrival, free date changes until that point.
- Office hours Mon–Sat, 08:00–18:00 EAT (UTC+3). Enquiries answered within one working day.

## Itineraries

### Northern Serengeti river crossings

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/safaris/northern-serengeti-river-crossings
- Type: Migration. Destination: Serengeti. Difficulty: Easy.
- Duration: 6 days, 5 nights.
- Price from: USD 3,450 per person sharing.
- Maximum group: 6. Meals: Full board. Vehicle: Private 4WD Land Cruiser.
- Rating: 4.9 from 128 reviews.
- Summary: The route runs Arusha to Kogatende, then works the Mara River line for three days. Crossings are unpredictable: herds gather at a bank for hours, then move in minutes. You spend full days at the river with a packed lunch rather than returning to camp at midday, which is what raises the odds of seeing one.
- Included: Park and concession fees for 5 nights; Full board accommodation; Private 4WD with pop-up roof and fridge; Arusha airport transfers; Drinking water, 2L per person per day.
- Not included: International flights; Tanzania visa (USD 50–100); Travel insurance; Balloon flight (USD 599); Tips.
- Day by day: Day 1, Arusha to Central Serengeti (Arusha to Seronera, 335 km); Day 2, Central Serengeti to Kogatende (Seronera to Kogatende, 140 km); Day 3, Mara River, full day (Kogatende to Kogatende, 60 km); Day 4, Lamai wedge and Kuria hills (Kogatende to Lamai, 75 km); Day 5, Kogatende to Ngorongoro rim (Kogatende to Ngorongoro, 290 km); Day 6, Crater descent and return to Arusha (Ngorongoro to Arusha, 190 km).

### Classic northern circuit

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/safaris/classic-northern-circuit
- Type: Wildlife. Destination: Tarangire, Ngorongoro, Serengeti. Difficulty: Easy.
- Duration: 7 days, 6 nights.
- Price from: USD 2,890 per person sharing.
- Maximum group: 6. Meals: Full board. Vehicle: Private 4WD Land Cruiser.
- Rating: 4.8 from 214 reviews.
- Summary: The standard northern loop, run at a slower pace than most operators: two nights per park instead of one, so you are not packing every morning. Covers 1,180 km in total.
- Included: All park fees; Full board accommodation; Private 4WD and English-speaking guide; Airport transfers.
- Not included: Flights; Visa; Insurance; Tips; Drinks.
- Day by day: Day 1, Arusha to Tarangire (Arusha to Tarangire, 120 km); Day 2, Tarangire full day (Tarangire to Tarangire, 85 km); Day 3, Tarangire to Serengeti (Tarangire to Seronera, 320 km); Day 4, Serengeti full day (Seronera to Seronera, 95 km); Day 5, Serengeti to Ngorongoro (Seronera to Ngorongoro, 215 km); Day 6, Ngorongoro Crater (Ngorongoro to Ngorongoro, 55 km); Day 7, Return to Arusha (Ngorongoro to Arusha, 190 km).

### Machame route, Kilimanjaro

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/safaris/machame-route-kilimanjaro
- Type: Trekking. Destination: Kilimanjaro. Difficulty: Challenging.
- Duration: 7 days, 6 nights.
- Price from: USD 2,150 per person sharing.
- Maximum group: 10. Meals: Full board on mountain. Vehicle: Transfer vehicle to gate.
- Rating: 4.7 from 96 reviews.
- Summary: Machame in seven days rather than six. The extra night at Karanga camp raises summit success from roughly 73% to 89% in our own 2024 figures. Summit night starts at 23:30 from Barafu.
- Included: Park and camping fees; Guides, cooks and porters; Tents and mess tent; All meals on the mountain; Two hotel nights in Moshi.
- Not included: Sleeping bag hire (USD 40); Flights; Visa; Tips (USD 250–300 per climber).
- Day by day: Day 1, Machame Gate to Machame Camp (Moshi to Machame Camp, 11 km); Day 2, Machame to Shira Camp (Machame Camp to Shira Camp, 5 km); Day 3, Shira to Barranco via Lava Tower (Shira Camp to Barranco Camp, 10 km); Day 4, Barranco to Karanga (Barranco Camp to Karanga Camp, 5 km); Day 5, Karanga to Barafu (Karanga Camp to Barafu Camp, 4 km); Day 6, Summit day (Barafu Camp to Uhuru Peak to Mweka, 17 km); Day 7, Mweka Gate to Moshi (Mweka Camp to Moshi, 10 km).

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/safaris/calving-season-ndutu

## Destinations

### Serengeti National Park

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/destinations/serengeti
- Region: Northern circuit. Best time: June to October, and February for calving.
- 14,750 km² of grassland and kopjes. Resident lion, leopard and cheetah year-round; the migration herds pass through the south in February and the north from July.
- Access: Eight hours by road from Arusha via Ngorongoro, or 1h20 by light aircraft to Seronera or Kogatende.
- Wildlife: Lion, Leopard, Cheetah, Wildebeest, Zebra, Spotted hyena, Giraffe, Elephant
- Key figures: Area 14,750 km², Lion population ~3,000, Park fee, per day $70, Drive from Arusha 8h.

### Ngorongoro Crater

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/destinations/ngorongoro
- Region: Conservation area. Best time: Year-round; drier June to October.
- A 260 km² caldera holding about 25,000 large animals, including one of the few reliable black rhino populations in Tanzania. The floor is reached by a single descent road.
- Access: Four hours by road from Arusha. One descent road in, one out, both gravel and 4WD only.
- Wildlife: Black rhino, Lion, Elephant, Buffalo, Flamingo, Golden jackal, Serval
- Key figures: Caldera floor 260 km², Rim altitude 2,286 m, Large animals ~25,000, Crater fee, per vehicle $295.

### Tarangire National Park

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/destinations/tarangire
- Region: Northern circuit. Best time: July to October.
- Baobab country, two and a half hours from Arusha. In the dry season the river holds the animals and elephant groups of over 100 are common.
- Access: Two and a half hours by road from Arusha on tar to the gate. The closest park to the city.
- Wildlife: Elephant, Lion, Leopard, Fringe-eared oryx, Lesser kudu, Yellow-collared lovebird
- Key figures: Area 2,850 km², Largest elephant group 100+, Bird species 550, Drive from Arusha 2h30.

### Mount Kilimanjaro

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/destinations/kilimanjaro
- Region: Kilimanjaro region. Best time: January to March, June to October.
- 5,895 m at Uhuru Peak, the highest point in Africa and the tallest free-standing mountain in the world. Seven established routes, no technical climbing required.
- Access: Ninety minutes by road from Arusha to Machame or Marangu gate; three hours to Londorossi for Lemosho.
- Wildlife: Colobus monkey, Blue monkey, Bushbuck, Hartlaub's turaco, White-necked raven
- Key figures: Summit 5,895 m, Established routes 7, Typical climb 6–9 days, Distance from Arusha 80 km.

### Zanzibar

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/destinations/zanzibar
- Region: Indian Ocean. Best time: June to October, December to February.
- An island 35 km off the coast, one hour by air from Arusha. Stone Town on the west, reef and white sand on the east and north-east.
- Access: One hour twenty by air from Arusha, or direct from Seronera airstrip so you skip the return drive.
- Wildlife: Green turtle, Bottlenose dolphin, Red colobus, Whale shark (Oct–Feb)
- Key figures: Distance offshore 35 km, Flight from Arusha 1h20, Reef at Mnemba 8 km out, Water temperature 26–29°C.

### Ndutu and the southern plains

- URL: https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/destinations/ndutu
- Region: Conservation area. Best time: January to March.
- Short-grass plains on the Serengeti–Ngorongoro boundary. The calving ground: roughly 500,000 wildebeest are born here across three weeks in February.
- Access: Six hours by road via Karatu, or fly to Ndutu airstrip. Off-road driving is permitted in the concession.
- Wildlife: Wildebeest, Cheetah, Lion, Spotted hyena, Golden jackal, Bat-eared fox
- Key figures: Calves born ~500,000, Peak births per day 8,000, Season Jan–Mar, Drive from Arusha 6h.

## Kilimanjaro

Summit is Uhuru Peak at 5,895 m. No technical climbing on any route.

### Machame route

- Approach: South-west. Nights: 6. Distance: 62 km.
- Summit success on our own departures: 89%.
- Sleeping: Tents. Scenery: Very high. Trail traffic: Busy.
- Price from USD 2,150 per climber.
- The climb-high-sleep-low profile at Lava Tower does the acclimatisation work. Steepest single section is the Barranco Wall, a scramble with no ropes.
- Best for: First-time climbers with six spare days who want the best success-to-cost ratio.
- Camp altitudes: Gate 1800 m, Machame 2835 m, Shira 3750 m, Lava Tower 4630 m, Barranco 3960 m, Karanga 3995 m, Barafu 4673 m, Uhuru 5895 m.

### Lemosho route

- Approach: West. Nights: 7. Distance: 70 km.
- Summit success on our own departures: 92%.
- Sleeping: Tents. Scenery: Very high. Trail traffic: Moderate.
- Price from USD 2,680 per climber.
- Two extra days on the Shira plateau before joining the Machame line. The longest approach, and the highest summit rate we run.
- Best for: Climbers who can spare eight days and want the widest acclimatisation margin.
- Camp altitudes: Londorossi 2100 m, Mti Mkubwa 2780 m, Shira 1 3610 m, Shira 2 3850 m, Lava Tower 4630 m, Barranco 3960 m, Karanga 3995 m, Barafu 4673 m, Uhuru 5895 m.

### Marangu route

- Approach: South-east. Nights: 5. Distance: 64 km.
- Summit success on our own departures: 68%.
- Sleeping: Huts. Scenery: Moderate. Trail traffic: Busy.
- Price from USD 1,890 per climber.
- The only route with dormitory huts and the only one you ascend and descend on the same path. Gentlest gradient, worst acclimatisation profile.
- Best for: Climbers who need a bed and a roof, or are travelling in the wettest months.
- Camp altitudes: Marangu Gate 1860 m, Mandara 2700 m, Horombo 3720 m, Kibo 4700 m, Uhuru 5895 m.

### Rongai route

- Approach: North. Nights: 6. Distance: 73 km.
- Summit success on our own departures: 81%.
- Sleeping: Tents. Scenery: High. Trail traffic: Quiet.
- Price from USD 2,340 per climber.
- The only approach from the Kenyan side. The northern slope sits in the rain shadow, so it stays driest when the south is wet.
- Best for: Climbing in the shoulder months, or wanting the fewest people on the trail.
- Camp altitudes: Nalemuru 1950 m, Simba 2625 m, Kikelewa 3600 m, Mawenzi Tarn 4330 m, Kibo 4700 m, Uhuru 5895 m.

## The Great Migration, month by month

The herd of roughly 1.5 million wildebeest and 300,000 zebra moves in a
continuous loop of about 800 km through the Serengeti and Mara ecosystem. It is
in Tanzania for roughly nine months of the year.

- Jan: Calving. Ndutu, southern plains. Herds settle on the short grass as the rains green it.
- Feb: Calving. Ndutu and Kusini. Around 8,000 calves born a day for three weeks.
- Mar: Calving. Southern Serengeti. Last calves drop; predators work the stragglers.
- Apr: On the move. Moru and Seronera. Long rains push the herds north-west in columns.
- May: On the move. Western corridor. The rut begins; columns stretch up to 40 km.
- Jun: River crossings. Grumeti River. First crossings at the Grumeti, with resident crocodile.
- Jul: Peak crossings. Northern Serengeti. Herds reach the Mara River line at Kogatende.
- Aug: Peak crossings. Mara River, Kogatende. Highest crossing frequency of the year.
- Sep: Peak crossings. Lamai wedge and Maasai Mara. Herds move back and forth across the river.
- Oct: River crossings. Northern Serengeti. Return crossings south as the north dries out.
- Nov: On the move. Lobo and Seronera. Short rains start; herds drift down the eastern side.
- Dec: On the move. Ndutu and eastern plains. Herds spread across the southern plains again.

## Frequently asked questions

### Before you book

**How far ahead should I book?**
Six to nine months for June–October and February. Three months is usually enough for April, May and November, when camps are quieter and rates drop.

**What is the deposit and when is the balance due?**
30% on confirmation, balance 45 days before arrival. Dates can be changed free of charge up to the 45-day point.

**Do you run group departures or private trips?**
Private only. Every itinerary is one vehicle for your party, with a maximum of six guests and a guaranteed window seat each.

**Can you build a route that is not listed?**
Yes. Roughly half of what we run is custom. Send the parks you want, your dates and a budget per person and we will draft a day-by-day plan.

### Money and paperwork

**What does a Tanzania visa cost?**
USD 50 for most nationalities, USD 100 for US passport holders. Apply online at the immigration e-services portal or on arrival at JRO.

**Are park fees included?**
Yes, on every listed itinerary. Serengeti is USD 70 per person per day, the Ngorongoro crater service fee is USD 295 per vehicle per descent, and both are priced into the quote.

**What should I budget for tips?**
USD 20–25 per guest per day for a safari guide. For Kilimanjaro, USD 250–300 per climber covers the whole crew and is pooled at the gate.

**Which currency and payment methods?**
Quotes are in USD. Bank transfer or card. Card payments carry a 3.5% processor fee, which we show on the invoice rather than folding into the price.

### On the ground

**Do I need vaccinations?**
Yellow fever proof is required only if you arrive from a country where it is endemic. Malaria prophylaxis is recommended for all safari areas below 1,800 m. Check with a travel clinic six weeks out.

**What is the luggage limit?**
Soft bags, 15 kg per person on domestic light aircraft. Vehicles have no practical limit, but the flights do, so pack to the 15 kg figure if your trip includes one.

**Is there phone signal and power?**
Vodacom and Airtel cover most of Seronera, Ngorongoro rim and Tarangire. The northern Serengeti is patchy. Every vehicle has 12V charging; camps run generators or solar, typically 06:00–10:00 and 18:00–23:00.

**What should I pack?**
Neutral layers, a fleece for the 6°C crater-rim mornings, closed shoes, sun hat, 8×42 binoculars and a dust-proof bag for camera bodies. Laundry is available at most lodges.

**Is it suitable for children?**
Yes from about six years old. Ngorongoro and Tarangire have the shortest drives. Some camps set a minimum age of 12 for walking activities, which we flag before you book.

## Field notes

- [When the Mara River crossings actually happen](https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/blog/when-mara-river-crossings-happen), 2026-06-12, by Emmanuel Kimaro. Crossings run from late June to late October, but the useful question is which bank to be sitting on. Here is what our 2023–2025 trip logs show.
- [Six or seven days on Machame: what the extra night buys](https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/blog/six-or-seven-days-on-machame), 2026-05-02, by Neema Laizer. The seven-day profile adds one night at Karanga at 3,995 m. In our own 2024 figures it moved summit success from 73% to 89%.
- [February in Ndutu: 8,000 calves a day and what follows them](https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/blog/february-in-ndutu), 2026-02-18, by Emmanuel Kimaro. Calving concentrates roughly 500,000 births into three weeks on the short-grass plains, and every predator in the ecosystem knows it.
- [What park fees actually cost in 2026](https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/blog/what-park-fees-actually-cost), 2026-01-20, by Neema Laizer. Park fees are 30–40% of a northern-circuit quote. Here is the line-by-line so you can check any operator's pricing, including ours.
- [Tarangire or Ngorongoro if you only have one day](https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/blog/choosing-between-tarangire-and-ngorongoro), 2025-11-08, by Emmanuel Kimaro. Both are within a half day of Arusha. They reward completely different trips, and the deciding factor is usually the month.
- [Packing for a northern circuit, by temperature](https://www.arushawildlifesafaris.com/blog/packing-for-a-northern-circuit), 2025-09-30, by Neema Laizer. The crater rim reaches 6°C before dawn and the Serengeti hits 30°C by midday. One trip, a 24-degree spread, one soft bag.
